claim: TAF7L is a paralogue of TFIID subunit TAF7.
source: Here we report that TAF7L, a paralogue of TFIID subunit TAF7, is enriched in adipocytes and white fat tissue (WAT) in mouse.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of TAF7L.

claim: TAF7L is enriched in adipocytes and white fat tissue (WAT) in mouse.
source: Here we report that TAF7L, a paralogue of TFIID subunit TAF7, is enriched in adipocytes and white fat tissue (WAT) in mouse.
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot and RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Depletion of TAF7L reduced adipocyte-specific gene expression.
source: Depletion of TAF7L reduced adipocyte-specific gene expression, compromised adipocyte differentiation, and WAT development as well.
evidence: This is supported by mRNA-seq data in Figure 3 and RT-qPCR data in Figure 2C showing reduced expression of adipocyte-specific genes upon TAF7L knockdown.

claim: Depletion of TAF7L compromised adipocyte differentiation.
source: Depletion of TAF7L reduced adipocyte-specific gene expression, compromised adipocyte differentiation, and WAT development as well.
evidence: This is supported by Oil red O staining in Figure 2B showing reduced adipocyte formation in TAF7L knockdown cells.

claim: Depletion of TAF7L compromised WAT development.
source: Depletion of TAF7L reduced adipocyte-specific gene expression, compromised adipocyte differentiation, and WAT development as well.
evidence: This is supported by histological analysis in Figure 4E showing reduced subcutaneous fat in Taf7l KO embryos and photographs in Figure 4F,G showing reduced fat pads in Taf7l KO mice.

claim: Ectopic expression of TAF7L in myoblasts reprograms these muscle precursors into adipocytes upon induction.
source: Ectopic expression of TAF7L in myoblasts reprograms these muscle precursors into adipocytes upon induction.
evidence: This is supported by Oil red O staining in Figure 5A showing lipid-laden cells in C2C12.TAF7L cells and mRNA-seq data in Figure 5D showing upregulation of adipocyte genes.

claim: TAF7L is required for activating adipocyte-specific genes via a dual mechanism wherein it interacts with PPARγ at enhancers and TBP/Pol II at core promoters.
source: Genome-wide mRNA-seq expression profiling and ChIP-seq binding studies confirmed that TAF7L is required for activating adipocyte-specific genes via a dual mechanism wherein it interacts with PPARγ at enhancers and TBP/Pol II at core promoters.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data in Figures 6 and 7 showing TAF7L binding at both promoters and enhancers, co-localization with PPARγ, TBP, and Pol II, and co-IP experiments in Figure 7E,G showing physical interactions.

claim: TAF7L forms complexes with both TBP and PPARγ in vitro.
source: In vitro binding studies confirmed that TAF7L forms complexes with both TBP and PPARγ.
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 7E,G.

claim: TBP and most canonical subunits of TFIID are down-regulated during C3H10T1/2 differentiation.
source: Consistent with the previous observations from 3T3-L1 adipogenesis studies (Guermah et al., 2003), our analysis of both protein and mRNA levels revealed that TBP and most of the canonical subunits of TFIID are down-regulated during C3H10T1/2 differentiation (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 1A and Western blot data in Figure 1B, and is consistent with previous published work.

claim: TAF7L is significantly up-regulated in differentiated C3H10T1/2 adipocytes.
source: Surprisingly however, one subunit (TAF7L) previously reported to be a component of TFIID primarily in testis (Pointud et al., 2003; Cheng et al., 2007) was found to be significantly up-regulated in differentiated C3H10T1/2 adipocytes (Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) and 3T3-L1 adipocytes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,C).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR and Western blot data in Figure 1A,B and supplemental figures, and references prior work on TAF7L in testis.

claim: TAF7L enrichment appears specific for the adipogenesis process since the mRNA abundance of Taf7l is downregulated to levels comparable to those of other TAF subunits during myogenesis.
source: Importantly, this enrichment appears specific for the adipogenesis process since the mRNA abundance of Taf7l is downregulated to levels comparable to those of other TAF subunits during myogenesis (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 1C showing Taf7l downregulation during myogenesis.

claim: Taf7l is most highly expressed in testis.
source: In concordance with previous studies, Taf7l is most highly expressed in testis (Pointud et al., 2003) (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR and Western blot data in Figure 1D,E and is consistent with previous published work.

claim: Taf7l shows significant expression in WAT and detectable expression in liver, spleen, brown adipose tissue (BAT) and kidney, but not in muscle or brain tissue.
source: Importantly, Taf7l also shows significant expression in WAT and detectable expression in liver, spleen, brown adipose tissue (BAT) and kidney, but not in muscle or brain tissue (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR and Western blot data in Figure 1D,E showing tissue-specific expression patterns.

claim: The expression of canonical TFIID subunits such as TAF4 is low in both WAT and muscle.
source: By contrast, the expression of canonical TFIID subunits such as TAF4 is low in both WAT and muscle as expected (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 1E.

claim: Taf7l-deficient mice show an impaired male fertility phenotype but no other defects were previously reported.
source: First, Taf7l had only been well documented to be critical for directing spermatogenesis in mice, and Taf7l-deficient mice show an impaired male fertility phenotype but no other defects were previously reported (Akinloye et al., 2007; Cheng et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous published work.

claim: Taf8 mRNA is down-regulated upon induction of C3H10T1/2 or 3T3-L1 cells to form adipocytes.
source: However, we have found Taf7l to be up-regulated while Taf8 mRNA is down-regulated upon induction of C3H10T1/2 or 3T3-L1 cells to form adipocytes (Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: shTAF7L significantly reduced TAF7L protein levels both pre- and post-adipogenesis.
source: As shown by Western blot, shTAF7L significantly reduced TAF7L protein levels both pre- and more dramatically post-adipogenesis while levels of canonical TFIID subunits remained largely unaltered in control and TAF7L knockdown pre-adipogenesis cultures (Figure 2A, pre-).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2A.

claim: Levels of canonical TFIID subunits remained largely unaltered in control and TAF7L knockdown pre-adipogenesis cultures.
source: As shown by Western blot, shTAF7L significantly reduced TAF7L protein levels both pre- and more dramatically post-adipogenesis while levels of canonical TFIID subunits remained largely unaltered in control and TAF7L knockdown pre-adipogenesis cultures (Figure 2A, pre-).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2A showing TAF4, TAF7, and TBP levels.

claim: The protein levels of the canonical TFIID subunits become largely decreased in control post-adipogenesis cultures.
source: Consistent with our previous observation in terminally differentiated cells, the protein levels of the canonical TFIID subunits become largely decreased in control post-adipogenesis cultures while cells that have been depleted of TAF7L and therefore blocked from differentiation show high levels of TFIID subunits.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2A (post-).

claim: Cells that have been depleted of TAF7L and therefore blocked from differentiation show high levels of TFIID subunits.
source: Consistent with our previous observation in terminally differentiated cells, the protein levels of the canonical TFIID subunits become largely decreased in control post-adipogenesis cultures while cells that have been depleted of TAF7L and therefore blocked from differentiation show high levels of TFIID subunits.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2A (post-).

claim: PPARγ levels increased in control shGFP cells post induction but showed markedly reduced levels in shTAF7L-treated cells.
source: As expected, PPARγ levels increased in control shGFP cells post induction but showed markedly reduced levels in shTAF7L-treated cells suggesting that TAF7L may directly or indirectly regulate this key adipogenic transcription factor.
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2A showing PPARγ levels.

claim: TAF7L may directly or indirectly regulate PPARγ.
source: As expected, PPARγ levels increased in control shGFP cells post induction but showed markedly reduced levels in shTAF7L-treated cells suggesting that TAF7L may directly or indirectly regulate this key adipogenic transcription factor.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that PPARγ levels are reduced when TAF7L is knocked down.

claim: shTAF7L efficiently reduced endogenous TAF7L levels and blocked adipogenesis without significantly affecting TFIID complex integrity.
source: Our results also suggest that shTAF7L efficiently reduced endogenous TAF7L levels and blocked adipogenesis without significantly affecting TFIID complex integrity (Figure 2A, post-).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data in Figure 2A showing maintained levels of other TFIID subunits.

claim: Very few lipid-laden adipocytes formed in TAF7L depleted C3H10T1/2 cells, whereas over 98% of shGFP-treated cells differentiated into mature adipocytes.
source: Very few lipid-laden adipocytes formed in TAF7L depleted C3H10T1/2 cells, whereas over 98% of shGFP-treated cells differentiated into mature adipocytes.
evidence: This is supported by Oil red O staining data in Figure 2B.

claim: The few adipocytes that formed in shTAF7L-treated cells appeared smaller and exhibited abnormal morphology compared to untreated or shGFP-treated C3H10T1/2 adipocytes.
source: The few adipocytes that formed in shTAF7L-treated cells appeared smaller and exhibited abnormal morphology compared to untreated or shGFP-treated C3H10T1/2 adipocytes (Figure 2B,E).
evidence: This is supported by microscopy images in Figure 2B,E.

claim: TAF7L knockdown largely compromised the adipogenic potential of C3H10T1/2 cells.
source: These results suggest that TAF7L knockdown largely compromised the adipogenic potential of C3H10T1/2 cells, thus functionally implicating TAF7L in adipocyte differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the Oil red O staining and gene expression data showing reduced adipocyte formation and adipocyte-specific gene expression.

claim: Introduction of TAF7LmA restored adipocyte formation in shTAF7L cells.
source: Our results indicate that introduction of TAF7LmA restored adipocyte formation (Figure 2E) and elevated expression of adipocyte-specific genes compared to vector control in shTAF7L cells (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is supported by Oil red O staining in Figure 2E and RT-qPCR data in Figure 2F.

claim: Overexpression of TAF7 failed to restore the adipogenic defects caused by the loss of TAF7L.
source: In contrast, overexpression of TAF7 failed to restore the adipogenic defects caused by the loss of TAF7L (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is supported by Oil red O staining in Figure 2E showing no rescue with TAF7.

claim: 2083 out of 2360 genes (88%) that are highly upregulated during adipocyte differentiation failed to be induced upon adipogenic induction in the absence of TAF7L.
source: Strikingly, 2083 out of 2360 genes (88%) that are highly upregulated during adipocyte differentiation failed to be induced upon adipogenic induction in the absence of TAF7L (Figure 3B,C).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 3B,C.

claim: The overall transcriptional profile of differentiated shTAF7L-treated C3H10T1/2 cells (shTAF7L-post) largely matched the expression levels of pre-differentiated C3H10T1/2 cells (10T1/2-pre) (R = 0.98).
source: Moreover, the overall transcriptional profile of differentiated shTAF7L-treated C3H10T1/2 cells (shTAF7L-post) largely matched the expression levels of pre-differentiated C3H10T1/2 cells (10T1/2-pre) (R = 0.98) (Figure 3B); while mature adipocytes (10T1/2-post) is distinct (R = 0.84) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA-seq correlation analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Loss of TAF7L in C3H10T1/2 cells severely impaired its adipogenic potential rendering shTAF7L-treated cells in an undifferentiated state.
source: Thus, loss of TAF7L in C3H10T1/2 cells severely impaired its adipogenic potential rendering shTAF7L-treated cells in an undifferentiated state (Figures 2B and 3A,B).
evidence: This is inferred from the Oil red O staining and mRNA-seq data showing lack of differentiation.

claim: Taf7l KO fibroblasts produced very few, if any, lipid-filled adipocytes compared to WT cells in response to adipogenic induction.
source: As revealed by Oil red O staining, Taf7l KO fibroblasts produced very few, if any, lipid-filled adipocytes compared to WT cells in response to adipogenic induction (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by Oil red O staining data in Figure 4A.

claim: Ablation of Taf7l suppresses the upregulation of adipocyte-specific genes during differentiation.
source: RT-qPCR analysis confirmed that ablation of Taf7l also suppresses the upregulation of adipocyte-specific genes during differentiation (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 4B.

claim: Loss of Taf7l caused no obvious change in mRNA or protein levels of other TFIID subunits.
source: As expected, loss of Taf7l caused no obvious change in mRNA or protein levels of other TFIID subunits (data not shown), suggesting that deletion of Taf7l is unlikely to affect TFIID integrity or function in vivo, in agreement with previous observations that Taf7l-deficient mice appear normal except for germ cell developmental defects (Cheng et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated based on unpublished data and is consistent with previous published work.

claim: FABP4+ lipid-laden cells are significantly diminished in the subcutaneous layer of Taf7l KO mice compared to WT littermate controls.
source: We observed that FABP4+ lipid-laden cells are significantly diminished in the subcutaneous layer of Taf7l KO mice compared to WT littermate controls with a concomittant increase in layers of connective-like tissue under the skin of Taf7l KO mice (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by H&E and FABP4 immunostaining data in Figure 4E.

claim: Loss of Taf7l impairs WAT development in the later stages of embryogenesis.
source: These results suggest that loss of Taf7l impairs WAT development in the later stages of embryogenesis (Gupta et al., 2010).
evidence: This is inferred from the histological data in E18.5 embryos and is consistent with cited work.

claim: In Taf7l-deficient mice, there may be an imbalance in mesodermal-derived lineages as revealed by the appearance of a thicker layer of subcutaneous connective-like tissue.
source: It also appears that in Taf7l-deficient mice, there may be an imbalance in mesodermal-derived lineages as revealed by the appearance of a thicker layer of subcutaneous connective-like tissue.
evidence: This is inferred from the histological observations in Figure 4E.

claim: 5 out of 12 Taf7l KO mice exhibited a noticeable reduction in both their subcutaneous and abdominal white fat pads compared to control WT animals.
source: The results revealed that 5 out of 12 Taf7l KO mice exhibited a noticeable reduction in both their subcutaneous and abdominal white fat pads compared to control WT animals (Figure 4F,G), while both groups consumed similar amounts of food and have similar growth curves (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is supported by photographs in Figure 4F,G and food intake/body weight data in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Taf7l KO and WT mice consumed similar amounts of food and have similar growth curves.
source: The results revealed that 5 out of 12 Taf7l KO mice exhibited a noticeable reduction in both their subcutaneous and abdominal white fat pads compared to control WT animals (Figure 4F,G), while both groups consumed similar amounts of food and have similar growth curves (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This is supported by food intake and body weight data in Figure 4C,D.

claim: A large proportion of C2C12.TAF7L cells developed into lipid-laden cells while no detectable C2C12.CNTL cells produced lipid droplets.
source: A large proportion of C2C12.TAF7L cells developed into lipid-laden cells while no detectable C2C12.CNTL cells produced lipid droplets (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by Oil red O staining data in Figure 5A.

claim: C2C12.TAF7L cells have markedly increased mRNA levels of a subset of adipocyte-specific genes including Adipsin, Resistin, Pparγ, C/EBPα, Adipoq and Fabp4 relative to C2C12.CNTL cells post differentiation.
source: Gene expression analysis by RT-qPCR confirmed that C2C12.TAF7L cells have markedly increased mRNA levels of a subset of adipocyte-specific genes including Adipsin, Resistin, Pparγ, C/EBPα, Adipoq and Fabp4 relative to C2C12.CNTL cells post differentiation (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C,E,F).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 5C and supplemental figures.

claim: Myoblast-gene Myf5 is downregulated in C2C12.TAF7L cells prior to and post adipogenic induction.
source: By contrast, myoblast-gene Myf5 is downregulated in C2C12.TAF7L cells prior to and post adipogenic induction (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: A number of adipocyte-specific genes become highly upregulated in C2C12.TAF7L cells compared to C2C12.CNTL cells post adipogenesis.
source: Furthermore, we performed mRNA-seq on differentiated C2C12.TAF7L and C2C12.CNTL cells and these genome-wide expression studies revealed that indeed, a number of adipocyte-specific genes become highly upregulated in C2C12.TAF7L cells compared to C2C12.CNTL cells post adipogenesis (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by mRNA-seq data in Figure 5D.

claim: ∼32% of genes upregulated fivefold or more in differentiated C2C12.TAF7L cells vs C2C12.CNTL cells are involved in either adipocyte differentiation or function.
source: Gene ontology analysis of genes upregulated fivefold or more in differentiated C2C12.TAF7L cells vs C2C12.CNTL cells indicated that ∼32% of these genes are involved in either adipocyte differentiation or function.
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: ∼10% of genes upregulated fivefold or more in differentiated C2C12.TAF7L cells vs C2C12.CNTL cells are involved in spermatogenesis and sexual reproduction.
source: Notably, in accordance with the role of Taf7l in spermatogenesis that was reported previously, ∼10% of these up-regulated genes are involved in spermatogenesis and sexual reproduction (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 5E and is consistent with previous work on TAF7L in spermatogenesis.

claim: Ectopic expression of TAF7L in C2C12 myoblasts, even at modestly elevated levels, is capable of inducing upregulation of Taf7l itself and other important adipogenic transcription factors including Pparγ and C/ebpα.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that ectopic expression of TAF7L in C2C12 myoblasts, even at modestly elevated levels, is capable of inducing upregulation of Taf7l itself and other important adipogenic transcription factors including Pparγ and C/ebpα (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C) thereby reprogramming a significant portion of C2C12 cells into adipocytes upon induction (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E,F), providing further evidence for TAF7L as a pro-adipogenic regulator.
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C.

claim: Only one significant TAF7L binding peak was identified in C3H10T1/2 cells compared to 18,672 significant TAF7L binding peaks detected after adipocyte formation.
source: In agreement with the low concentration of TAF7L shown in Western blots prior to differentiation (Figure 1A), only one significant peak was identified in C3H10T1/2 cells compared to 18,672 significant TAF7L binding peaks detected after adipocyte formation.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: Comparably large numbers of peaks for TBP (12,883 and 14,587) and Pol II (14,502 and 11,424) were found in pre- and post-differentiation C3H10T1/2 cells.
source: At the same time, we found comparably large numbers of peaks for TBP (12,883 and 14,587) and Pol II (14,502 and 11,424) in pre- and post-differentiation C3H10T1/2 cells.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: TAF7L binds to >65% of adipocyte-specific genes that are highly upregulated (>50×) during adipogenesis.
source: Analysis of our ChIP-seq and mRNA-seq data suggests that among all active genes in adipocytes, TAF7L binds to >65% of adipocyte-specific genes that are highly upregulated (>50×) during adipogenesis while binding much less frequently at both core promoters (<500 bp from TSS) and proximal enhancer regions (500 bp to 5 kb from TSS) near genes unaltered or downregulated during differentiation (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq and mRNA-seq data analysis shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The average TAF7L binding strength on genes upregulated >50× is twice as strong as on genes induced between 5–50× in adipocytes relative to C3H10T1/2 cells, and eight times stronger than on genes down-regulated following adipogenesis.
source: For instance, examination of 3,468 TAF7L peaks, representing 20% of the total peaks located at proximal enhancers revealed that the average TAF7L binding strength on genes upregulated >50× is twice as strong as on genes induced between 5–50× in adipocytes relative to C3H10T1/2 cells, and eight times stronger than on genes down-regulated following adipogenesis (Figure 6D), suggesting that TAF7L binding frequency and strength is highly correlated with upregulated genes during adipogenesis.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: TAF7L binding frequency and strength is highly correlated with upregulated genes during adipogenesis.
source: For instance, examination of 3,468 TAF7L peaks, representing 20% of the total peaks located at proximal enhancers revealed that the average TAF7L binding strength on genes upregulated >50× is twice as strong as on genes induced between 5–50× in adipocytes relative to C3H10T1/2 cells, and eight times stronger than on genes down-regulated following adipogenesis (Figure 6D), suggesting that TAF7L binding frequency and strength is highly correlated with upregulated genes during adipogenesis.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Both TBP and Pol II display greater than 63% occupancy at transcriptional start sites (TSS) of highly expressed genes in both undifferentiated C3H10T1/2 cells and adipocytes.
source: By mapping the genomic binding sites, we found that both TBP and Pol II display greater than 63% occupancy at transcriptional start sites (TSS) of highly expressed genes in both undifferentiated C3H10T1/2 cells and adipocytes, consistent with their roles in mediating global and general transcription functions.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis and is consistent with known functions of TBP and Pol II.

claim: TAF7L only partially (30%) colocalizes with TBP and Pol II at a subset of promoters, while a greater proportion (45%) of TAF7L peaks localizes to enhancer regions where TBP and Pol II are generally not found.
source: Interestingly, comparing the binding regions of TAF7L, TBP and Pol II in adipocytes revealed that TAF7L only partially (30%) colocalizes with TBP and Pol II at a subset of promoters, while a greater proportion (45%) of TAF7L peaks localizes to enhancer regions where TBP and Pol II are generally not found (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 7B,C.

claim: TAF7L may function via additional mechanisms other than as a subunit of canonical TFIID in regulating adipocyte differentiation.
source: This surprising finding suggests that TAF7L may function via additional mechanisms other than as a subunit of canonical TFIID in regulating adipocyte differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that TAF7L localizes to enhancers where TBP and Pol II are not found.

claim: DNA consensus sequence motifs enriched in TAF7L peaks include binding motifs of well-known adipogenic transcription factors including PPARγ and C/EBPγ.
source: We analyzed the sequences surrounding TAF7L binding sites and identified several DNA consensus sequence motifs enriched in TAF7L peaks. Next, we compared these motifs with all known sequence-specific recognition elements of transcription factors, which led to the identification of several binding motifs of well-known adipogenic transcription factors including PPARγ and C/EBPγ (Ge et al., 2008) (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is supported by motif analysis shown in Figure 7A and is consistent with cited work.

claim: 4,121 and 12,893 significant peaks for PPARγ were detected in C3H10T1/2 cells pre- and post-differentiation, respectively.
source: We then used ChIP-seq to directly map the genome-wide binding profiles of PPARγ and detected 4,121 and 12,893 significant peaks for PPARγ in C3H10T1/2 cells pre- and post-differentiation, respectively.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: The majority of PPARγ binding sites mapped overlap with those previously reported in 3T3-L1 derived adipocytes.
source: We then validated our ChIP-seq data by comparing our new data with published ChIP-seq data for PPARγ, C/EBPα, and RXRα in 3T3-L1 derived adipocytes 6 days post-differentiation (Mikkelsen et al., 2010; Schmidt et al., 2011; Waki et al., 2011). This extensive analysis revealed that the majority of PPARγ binding sites we mapped overlap with those previously reported although some differences in specific binding sites were observed, likely due to inherent differences between 3T3-L1 and C3H10T1/2 cells.
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published ChIP-seq data.

claim: 26% of TAF7L peaks were co-occupied by PPARγ and reciprocally, 37% of PPARγ peaks were co-bound by TAF7L.
source: A direct comparison of TAF7L and PPARγ genome-wide binding profiles revealed that 26% of TAF7L peaks were co-occupied by PPARγ and reciprocally, 37% of PPARγ peaks were co-bound by TAF7L (Figure 7B,D).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis shown in Figure 7B,D.

claim: TAF7L binds to 20% of RXRα bound loci genome-wide.
source: Similarly, TAF7L binds to 20% of RXRα bound loci genome-wide.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: TAF7L co-localizes with 25% of C/EBPα binding and vice versa.
source: Moreover, TAF7L also co-localizes with 25% of C/EBPα binding and vice versa.
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq data analysis.

claim: There is a functional association between TAF7L and adipogenic activators PPARγ, RXRα and C/EBPα in adipocytes.
source: Collectively, these findings provide indirect evidence for a functional association between TAF7L and adipogenic activators PPARγ, RXRα and C/EBPα in adipocytes.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-localization data from ChIP-seq.

claim: TAF7L might also functions as an enhancer-associated co-activator that connects adipogenic activators with the core promoter recognition machinery to potentiate adipocyte differentiation.
source: Indeed, the relationship between TAF7L, PPARγ, C/EBPα and TBP/Pol II at a genome-wide scale suggests that TAF7L might also functions as an enhancer-associated co-activator that connects adipogenic activators with the core promoter recognition machinery to potentiate adipocyte differentiation.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq data showing TAF7L co-localization with both enhancer-binding factors and core promoter machinery.

claim: PPARγ can efficiently pull down TAF7L and vice versa with or without the addition of PPARγ ligand rosiglitozone.
source: Intriguingly, these co-IP assays showed that PPARγ can efficiently pull down TAF7L and vice versa with (data not shown) or without the addition of PPARγ ligand rosiglitozone (Figure 7E); by contrast, PPARγ was unable to co-IP TBP (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is supported by co-IP data in Figure 7E.

claim: PPARγ was unable to co-IP TBP.
source: Intriguingly, these co-IP assays showed that PPARγ can efficiently pull down TAF7L and vice versa with (data not shown) or without the addition of PPARγ ligand rosiglitozone (Figure 7E); by contrast, PPARγ was unable to co-IP TBP (Figure 7F).
evidence: This is supported by co-IP data in Figure 7F.

claim: TAF7L and TBP can pull down each other reciprocally.
source: As expected, TAF7L and TBP can pull down each other reciprocally (Figure 7G), which is consistent with previous observations (Pointud et al., 2003).
evidence: This is supported by co-IP data in Figure 7G and is consistent with previous published work.

claim: The association between TAF7L and PPARγ or TBP is direct and not mediated via DNA/chromatin interactions.
source: To confirm that the association between TAF7L and PPARγ or TBP is direct and not mediated via DNA/chromatin interactions, we included benzonase treatment in our co-IP assays. Eliminating DNA in these co-IP experiments did not alter the binding interactions we observed between TAF7L and PPARγ or TBP (data now shown).
evidence: This is supported by benzonase-treated co-IP experiments (data not shown).

claim: Over-expression of TAF7L in C3H10T1/2 cells and adipocytes allows co-IP of other endogenous TFIID subunits including TBP and TAF4.
source: As expected, over-expression of TAF7L in C3H10T1/2 cells and adipocytes allows co-IP of other endogenous TFIID subunits including TBP and TAF4 (data not shown), suggesting that some tagged-TAF7L can integrate into native TFIID complexes.
evidence: This is supported by co-IP experiments (data not shown).

claim: Some tagged-TAF7L can integrate into native TFIID complexes.
source: As expected, over-expression of TAF7L in C3H10T1/2 cells and adipocytes allows co-IP of other endogenous TFIID subunits including TBP and TAF4 (data not shown), suggesting that some tagged-TAF7L can integrate into native TFIID complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-IP data showing TAF7L can pull down other TFIID subunits.

claim: TAF7L can physically associate with both PPARγ and TBP/TFIID either directly or indirectly via presently unidentified protein factors.
source: Taken together, these protein:protein binding assays suggest that TAF7L can physically associate with both PPARγ and TBP/TFIID either directly or indirectly via presently unidentified protein factors.
evidence: This is inferred from the co-IP data.

claim: TAF7L may serve as a cofactor linking specific adipogenic activators, proximal enhancers and the core transcription apparatus.
source: These studies provide a potential mechanism by which TAF7L may serve as a cofactor linking specific adipogenic activators, proximal enhancers and the core transcription apparatus.
evidence: This is inferred from the ChIP-seq and co-IP data showing TAF7L interactions with both enhancer-binding factors and core promoter machinery.

claim: Increased numbers of adipocytes, a major underlying cause of obesity, are primarily derived from MSCs and/or ASCs.
source: Given that increased numbers of adipocytes, a major underlying cause of obesity, are primarily derived from MSCs and/or ASCs (Bowers and Lane, 2008), we chose C3H10T1/2 MSCs as our cell culture model system for studying adipogenesis in large measure because MSCs efficiently recapitulate aspects of adipocyte differentiation and in vivo fat development.
evidence: This is based on citation to previous published work.

claim: MSCs efficiently recapitulate aspects of adipocyte differentiation and in vivo fat development.
source: Given that increased numbers of adipocytes, a major underlying cause of obesity, are primarily derived from MSCs and/or ASCs (Bowers and Lane, 2008), we chose C3H10T1/2 MSCs as our cell culture model system for studying adipogenesis in large measure because MSCs efficiently recapitulate aspects of adipocyte differentiation and in vivo fat development.
evidence: This is stated as justification for the choice of cell model.

claim: TAF7L plays an integral role in adipocyte gene expression by targeting enhancers as a cofactor for PPARγ and promoters as a component of the core transcriptional machinery.
source: These findings suggest that TAF7L plays an integral role in adipocyte gene expression by targeting enhancers as a cofactor for PPARγ and promoters as a component of the core transcriptional machinery.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from the ChIP-seq, co-IP, and functional data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Energy storage and metabolic homeostasis are tightly related/linked to reproductive abilities since both are highly sensitive to and dependent on nutrient availability.
source: For example, one can speculate that energy storage and metabolic homeostasis are tightly related/linked to reproductive abilities since both are highly sensitive to and dependent on nutrient availability (Vernon et al., 1986; Hashmi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is presented as speculation supported by citations.

claim: Steroid hormones (i.e. testosterone), which are essential for spermatogenesis, are derived from cholesterol.
source: Another possible link involved steroid hormones (i.e. testosterone), which are essential for spermatogenesis, are derived from cholesterol (Chowdhury and Mukherjee, 1976; Mahmoud et al., 1985).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous published work.

claim: Genome-wide mRNA-seq expression analysis identified Taf7l-mediated enrichment of genes involved in both adipogenesis and reproductive processes.
source: In any case, our genome-wide mRNA-seq expression analysis unambiguously identified Taf7l-mediated enrichment of genes involved in both adipogenesis and reproductive processes.
evidence: This is supported by mRNA-seq data and gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: TAF7L binds to and regulates the expression of a subset of white adipose genes.
source: Our data clearly showed that TAF7L binds to and regulates the expression of a subset of white adipose genes, interestingly we also observed downregulation of some brown adipocyte genes (Cidea, Ucp1 and Elovl3) caused by TAF7L knockdown (Figure 2C) (Kajimura et al., 2009; Kajimura et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by ChIP-seq and RT-qPCR data in Figure 2C and is consistent with cited work.

claim: Taf7l-deficient mice showed changed serum glucose levels after 24 hr fasting compared with control WT littermates.
source: Further, our preliminary attempts to measure metabolic functions suggest that Taf7l-deficient mice showed changed serum glucose levels after 24 hr fasting compared with control WT littermates, it will be interesting to explore whether and how Taf7l KO alters energy metabolism.
evidence: This is stated as a preliminary observation.

claim: Adipose tissue plays a central role in energy homeostasis by acting as a major lipid storage site as well as an important endocrine tissue.
source: Adipose tissue plays a central role in energy homeostasis by acting as a major lipid storage site as well as an important endocrine tissue.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Excess food intake vs energy expenditure invariably leads to obesity.
source: Excess food intake vs energy expenditure invariably leads to obesity, an increasingly prevalent condition in modern societies.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Obesity is tightly associated with an elevated risk of type-2 diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and certain cancers.
source: Obesity is, in turn, tightly associated with an elevated risk of type-2 diabetes, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and certain cancers, posing serious public health issues and rapidly escalating costs of health care (Rosen and MacDougald, 2006; Rosen and Spiegelman, 2006).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous published work.

claim: Accumulation of adipose tissue mass results from increase in both adipocyte size and number.
source: Accumulation of adipose tissue mass results from increase in both adipocyte size and number.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: The size of adipocytes depends on the amount of stored lipids.
source: The size of adipocytes depends on the amount of stored lipids, while an increase in adipocyte number (adipogenesis) generally results from the expansion of adult precursor cells and subsequent differentiation, an underlying cause of obesity (Rosen and MacDougald, 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: An increase in adipocyte number (adipogenesis) generally results from the expansion of adult precursor cells and subsequent differentiation, an underlying cause of obesity.
source: The size of adipocytes depends on the amount of stored lipids, while an increase in adipocyte number (adipogenesis) generally results from the expansion of adult precursor cells and subsequent differentiation, an underlying cause of obesity (Rosen and MacDougald, 2006).
evidence: This is based on citation to previous published work.

claim: Key adipogenic transcriptional activators such as C/EBPα and PPARγ were identified using well-established in vitro cell models.
source: The utilization of these model cells identified key adipogenic transcriptional activators such as C/EBPα and PPARγ (Hu et al., 1995; Brun et al., 1996; Tang et al., 2003; Zhang et al., 2004b).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous published work.

claim: Other transcription factors and cofactors, such as KLF15, KLF9, MED1, MED14, MED15, MED23 and TAF8, have been reported to be involved in either adipocyte commitment or differentiation in model cell lines.
source: Other transcription factors and cofactors, such as KLF15, KLF9, MED1, MED14, MED15, MED23 and TAF8, have also been reported to be involved in either adipocyte commitment or differentiation in model cell lines (Guermah et al., 2003; Mori et al., 2005; Matsumoto et al., 2007; Wang et al., 2009; Grøntved et al., 2010; Pei et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous published work.

claim: Adipocyte-specific expression signatures and genome-wide binding maps of pro-adipogenic activators such as PPARγ, C/EBPα, and RXRα have been primarily determined from 3T3-L1 derived adipocytes.
source: Specifically, adipocyte-specific expression signatures and genome-wide binding maps of pro-adipogenic activators such as PPARγ, C/EBPα, and RXRα have been primarily determined from 3T3-L1 derived adipocytes.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Other factors, including ZFP423, NF1 family proteins, and IRFs have been implicated in adipogenesis.
source: Other factors, including ZFP423, NF1 family proteins, and IRFs have been also implicated in adipogenesis (Eguchi et al., 2008; Mikkelsen et al., 2010; Schmidt et al., 2011; Waki et al., 2011; Boergesen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous published work.

claim: The full complement of key transcriptional regulators that orchestrate adipogenesis remains to be illucidated.
source: However, it has become evident that the full complement of key transcriptional regulators that orchestrate adipogenesis remains to be illucidated.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: TAF4b is a key component in the development of the mouse ovary and spermatogenesis.
source: The examples of these include TAF4b which was found to be a key component in the development of the mouse ovary and spermatogenesis (Freiman et al., 2001; Voronina et al., 2007), and TAF3 which was found to be required for mouse germ-layer differentiation (Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous published work.

claim: TAF3 is required for mouse germ-layer differentiation.
source: The examples of these include TAF4b which was found to be a key component in the development of the mouse ovary and spermatogenesis (Freiman et al., 2001; Voronina et al., 2007), and TAF3 which was found to be required for mouse germ-layer differentiation (Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is based on citation to previous published work.

claim: A TRF3/TAF3 complex is important for mouse myogenesis and zebrafish hematopoiesis.
source: Additionally, a TRF3/TAF3 complex was found to be important for mouse myogenesis and zebrafsh hematopoiesis (Deato et al., 2008; Hart et al., 2009).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous published work.

claim: TAF8 was reported as a component of TFIID implicated in adipocyte formation using 3T3-L1 cells.
source: With respect to adipogenesis, the only hint of such a mechanism came from previous studies of TAF8, which was reported as a component of TFIID implicated in adipocyte formation using 3T3-L1 cells (Guermah et al., 2003).
evidence: This is based on citation to previous published work.
